ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
otp_present: functionally — the 32-bit DPIDR (IDCODE) register + TARGETID + DLPIDR + AP IDR registers are functionally OTP-equivalent (hard-wired at silicon mask level, read-only via the SWD bus), although ADIv5 does not call them OTP. There is no fuse-bank or programmable OTP at the SWD protocol layer itself; per-vendor extensions add JTAG/SWD-disable fuses that are programmed at production test.

dpidr_register_content.access: Read-only via SWD Request(APnDP=0, RnW=1, A[2:3]=0); parallel-loaded at silicon mask level; shifted out via SWDIO on each IDCODE read transaction.

field_map.name: REVISION
field_map.description: Silicon revision identifier of the DP design (designer-defined; mask-set-time fixed).

field_map.name: DESIGNER
field_map.description: JEP106 designer ID (7-bit identity + 4-bit continuation count). Arm's JEP106 is 0x23B (continuation=4, identity=0x3B).

field_map.name: RAO
field_map.description: Read-As-One; hard-wired to 1 so a stuck-low SWDIO is distinguishable from a real DPIDR.

targetid_register_content.access: Read-only via DP bank 2 (SELECT.DPBANKSEL=2; read A[2:3]=0x4); parallel-loaded at silicon mask level.

dlpidr_register_content.access: Read-only via DP bank 3 (SELECT.DPBANKSEL=3; read A[2:3]=0x4); parallel-loaded at silicon mask level.

field_map.name: TINSTANCE
field_map.description: Multi-drop target instance number (1..15 if multiple SoCs share a 2-wire SWD bus).

field_map.name: PROTVSN
field_map.description: Multi-drop SWD protocol version (0001 = ADIv5.2 SWD).

ap_idr_register_content.applicable_when: Each AP implements its own 32-bit IDR (offset 0xFC).

usercode_or_user_otp_content.applicable_when: Vendor-specific. Some SoCs implement a USERCODE-like 32-bit register reachable via a vendor-specific MEM-AP system-bus address. ADIv5 does not standardize this.
usercode_or_user_otp_content.writability: Vendor-defined; sometimes loaded from on-chip fuses at boot.

vendor_jtag_swd_disable_fuses.applicable_when: Many production SoCs implement a one-way fuse that disables or restricts the SWD interface (e.g. ST RDP Level 2, Nordic UICR.APPROTECT, NXP DCFG, ESP32 efuse JTAG_DISABLE). These are NOT part of ADIv5 but are layered on top.
common_behaviors: Full SWD disable — fuse blown post-production; the SWD pads no longer respond.
ROM-only access — fuse limits MEM-AP access to a ROM region; flash + RAM are not visible.
Mass-erase-only — fuse forces a mass-erase before any debug access is granted (host can recover the SoC for re-programming, but cannot read out existing flash contents).

notes: ADIv5 mandates DPIDR (the DP IDCODE) but treats TARGETID, DLPIDR, EVENTSTAT, and the AP IDRs as identification registers — all read-only and effectively ROM at the SoC's silicon mask level. There is no protocol-defined writable OTP at the SWD layer. Per-vendor security extensions (JTAG/SWD-disable fuses, RDP levels, secure-boot enrolment registers) are layered on top of the standard but vary by silicon vendor.
